adverse_media.summary: The Paris prosecutor's JUNALCO unit opened a judicial investigation, led by an investigating judge, into Binance. It covers aggravated money laundering, laundering of tax-fraud and drug-trafficking proceeds, and illegal practice as a crypto-asset service provider (PSAN), for conduct in France and the EU from 2019 to 2024. The alleged failings are unlawful advertising (including through influencers) and AML/KYC failures. It follows a preliminary investigation opened in 2022 and widened in June 2023. Binance denies the allegations.
adverse_media.status: Ongoing. I found no charges (mise en examen) as of 2026-11-01.

adverse_media.summary: The AMF removed Binance France SAS from the PSAN register (E2022-037) automatically when the MiCA transitional period ended, as it had no MiCA authorisation. Binance says it is working to obtain one. ESMA and national regulators (France, Germany, Greece) are reportedly reviewing Binance's use of the reverse-solicitation exemption.
The ACPR carried out on-site AML/CFT inspections of crypto firms including Binance from late 2024, and reportedly told Binance to strengthen its risk controls. Binance called the inspections routine.

The AMF had warned Binance France (December 2023) that it must act on beneficial-owner issues after Changpeng Zhao's US cases (DOJ, CFTC, FinCEN; guilty plea November 2023). Ownership then moved to two new 50/50 beneficial owners (Lihua He, Yulong Yan), about whom little is public.
French investors sued Binance France and Binance Holdings Limited over more than €2.4m in losses, alleging misleading commercial practices and fraudulent concealment.

output.risk_rationale: Binance France SAS (SIREN 905060109) is an active French SAS at 1 Rue de Stockholm, Paris. It reported €53.1m revenue and €11.8m net profit for 2025 (INSEE/recherche-entreprises, as_of 2026-11-10). Its LEI has lapsed. Neither the entity nor its directors (David Princay, Christelle Tang) or reported beneficial owners (Lihua He, Yulong Yan) match any OFAC SDN, UK OFSI or EU consolidated sanctions entry, and none is identified as a PEP. The rating is still high for four reasons. First, since January 2025 a Paris investigating judge has been running a criminal investigation into Binance for aggravated money laundering (including drug and tax-fraud proceeds) and illegal PSAN activity from 2019 to 2024, and it is ongoing. Second, the company lost its AMF PSAN registration on 2 July 2026 and had no MiCA authorisation as of November 2026, so it currently has no licence to serve French clients. Third, the ACPR found AML/CFT control weaknesses in 2024–25. Fourth, the AMF required the 2023–24 ownership restructuring to remove Changpeng Zhao after his US guilty plea, and the new 50/50 beneficial owners are opaque and not verified on the official register. Group-level US enforcement against Binance Holdings and French investor litigation add to the risk.
